summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory (mode 1777, owner root:root) so all users can write into it but only file owners (or root) can remove their own files, using the standard sticky-bit mechanism. Verified functionally before and after a full node reboot, and confirmed the reboot via a changed kernel boot_id.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 7.9) baseline: /srv existed empty, sudo available non-interactively
Created /srv/drop, set ownership root:root and mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt) enabling shared write + sticky-bit delete restriction
Created temporary test users dropuserA/dropuserB to functionally verify: dropuserA could write a file, dropuserB was denied removing it (Operation not permitted), dropuserA (owner) could remove it
Cleaned up test users and test file after verification
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and /srv/drop config/permissions
Triggered a background-acknowledged 'shutdown -r now' reboot on node1
Polled node1 until it came back online (initial poll timed out as expected mid-reboot, follow-up succeeded)
Confirmed boot_id changed from 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f to df76a1d0-6d86-4c46-a6b8-0a6b8156ab2f, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart that /srv/drop retained mode 1777 and sticky-bit delete-restriction behavior still functioned correctly, then cleaned up test artifacts again

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as shared writable directory with sticky-bit protection (mode 1777)
evidence.summary: stat shows /srv/drop as drwxrwxrwt root:root immediately after creation

evidence.requirement: Functional proof users cannot remove files owned by other users, but can remove their own
evidence.summary: Created test users dropuserA/dropuserB; dropuserA wrote a file, dropuserB's rm attempt failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1), while dropuserA successfully removed its own file afterward

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of temporary test users used only for verification
evidence.summary: userdel removed dropuserA and dropuserB; getent confirmed no residual entries

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline for node1 (boot identity + service/data state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f and confirmed /srv/drop mode drwxrwxrwt root:root prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: sudo shutdown -r now issued via backgrounded nohup; command returned 'ack' immediately before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity), not just elapsed time
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down during reboot); second poll succeeded with a new boot_id df76a1d0-6d86-4c46-a6b8-0a6b8156ab2f, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit delete-restriction behavior
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/drop still shows drwxrwxrwt root:root; recreated test users confirmed dropuserB again denied removing dropuserA's file (Operation not permitted) while owner could remove it; test artifacts cleaned up
